text:
maria (Sales): Quick sync — DeltaHealth wants a short POC to validate throughput for their patient-chat product. They expect ~250k reqs/day with heavy burst windows: ~900 rps sustained for 10–15 min, avg prompt+response ~900 tokens, 95th-latency target <250ms. Can we draft a capacity plan + pricing ballpark?

jake (SE): Ok noted. My quick read: with 900 rps at ~900 tokens we should optimize for batching + KV cache reuse. Recommended POC setup: two model variants (fp16 and int4 quant) behind a routing policy. Start with 3 mid-sized GPUs for baseline + burst pool up to 6 GPUs. Prewarm policy to keep at least 2 GPUs hot to avoid repeated cold starts.

maria (Sales): Any rough cost numbers we can give the AE for initial ask? They want to know if committed vs reserved changes economics.

jake (SE): Ballpark for the POC (hosted, 3 baseline GPUs + burst to 6): ~$12k/month baseline for committed capacity + estimated $1.8k per extra GPU-month when bursting. For committed contract (6 dedicated GPUs) you'd see ~35–45% unit cost reduction vs on-demand. Exact depends on avg token count and prefix cache hit rate.

nina (SRE): A few operational notes:
- autoscale by concurrent streams (not raw rps) to respect KV cache and batching efficiencies.
- prewarm window 5–10m, cooldown 3–5m to avoid oscillation.
- enforce node draining with in-flight request grace.
- monitor prefix cache hit rate and token-per-request distribution; cache hit >30% changes GPU needs a lot.

Also watch the maximum sequence length — 900 tokens + kv overhead can push memory; if they attach embeddings/rerank during the flow we'll need larger instances or lower batch sizes.

sam (Product): Enterprise blocker to flag: DeltaHealth requires an IP allowlist + egress control and wants KMS-managed keys. If we keep this in hosted, we need to validate their security questionnaire answers. They may prefer a Private deployment for data residency. That impacts capacity (on-prem GPUs) and pricing.

maria (Sales): Good call. For the POC we should offer two paths: hosted POC with dedicated pool + allowlist and private POC as an option. Jake, can you share a minimal autoscale config we can propose?

jake (SE): Pasted a trimmed config sketch for the SRE/ops team to review:
```json
{
  "policy": "custom",
  "min_instances": 2,
  "max_instances": 6,
  "scale_metric": "concurrent_streams",
  "scale_thresholds": {
    "scale_up_concurrent": 120,
    "scale_down_concurrent": 60
  },
  "prewarm_seconds": 300,
  "cooldown_seconds": 240
}
```
Notes: thresholds will be tuned after one week of telemetry. Use quantized model for burst path to reduce memory/latency.

maria (Sales): Nice. Nina — what telemetry should we capture during the POC so sales can decide commit sizing?

nina (SRE): Minimum metrics: 95th token generation latency, 95th end-to-end latency, tokens/sec per GPU, avg batch size, KV cache hit rate, error/retry counts, GPU utilization (p99), and cost per 1M tokens. Also capture peak concurrent streams and peak seq length distribution.

maria (Sales): Perfect. I also need a short answer for the security questionnaire Q: "How do you ensure predictable throughput and isolation for enterprise commitments?" Any concise wording?

jake (SE): Draft: "We provide Dedicated pools (customer-isolated GPU nodes) with configurable autoscale policies, prewarming, and traffic routing to model variants. For enterprise commits we recommend a baseline reserved pool sized from POC telemetry; the platform supports KMS integration, VPC peering, and IP allowlists to meet isolation requirements."

maria (Sales): Great — I'll paste that. One more: DeltaHealth wants a 2-month POC, then decision. Can we propose a 2-month reserved trial: 2 reserved GPUs baseline, burst to 6, billing pro-rated?

jake (SE): Yes, propose 2-month reserved with an option to convert to a 12‑month commit. SLA will be our standard Dedicated SLA; if they need stricter SLOs we can scope an enterprise SLA addendum.

deploy-bot: Created ticket INF-4821 to track DeltaHealth POC capacity, autoscale config, and security questionnaire answers.

maria (Sales): Thanks team — I'll confirm with DeltaHealth and schedule a short tech-POC kickoff next Tue. Action items: Jake to finalize POC pricing lines and config, Nina to prepare telemetry dashboard template, Sam to gather security questionnaire attachments. I'll update INF-4821 with timeline. :thumbsup:
